correctness.rationale: For an idempotent, torsion vanishing is equivalent to both image and kernel being Lie subalgebras. All subalgebras of a codimension-one abelian extension are classified by the invariant intersection and a lift. The three exhaustive and disjoint projection-lift configurations yield exact Gaussian counts; the deficient eigenspace and (q-1)q^{2n} lift factor are proved and checked. In characteristic two the bracket of any two vectors lies in their span, making every subspace a subalgebra. Standard uniform Gaussian-binomial bounds prove the odd vs even quadratic exponents. Independent exhaustive direct torsion matrices and complementary-subalgebra pair enumerations matched the formula for specified prime-field cases. The general theorem rests on proof, not those samples.

value.rationale: Integrable idempotent Nijenhuis operators parametrize compatible Lie subalgebra splittings, a natural structural object. A pair of opposing adjoint eigenvalues creates nontrivial invariant-subspace constraints, while their merger in characteristic two removes all torsion restrictions. The complete operator-rank distribution, not just sample counts, identifies a quadratic-exponent scarcity q^{-n^2/2+O_q(n)} in odd characteristic versus exact abundance in even characteristic. This is a meaningful characteristic boundary in an infinite Lie family; Gaussian counts and the generic splitting criterion are explicitly prior ingredients.
